items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Even George Primrose, he wasn't no tap dancer, you see? But I mean, that was the most happy medium, it was the most popular.

ctx.x: But you were mentioning white performers that were doing it. Eleanor Powell, George M. Cohan.

She was a student. I mean she was a great dancer, but she wasn't no great tap dancer. She was becoming a great tap dancer from Mr. Buddy Bradley. See? I mentioned the great tap dancers in the whites was like Tom Patricola, James Barton, Walter Huston, people like that, men. George Murphy. And George M. Cohan. Even George Primrose, he wasn't no tap dancer, you see? But I mean, that was the most happy medium, it was the most popular. It was more popular than jazz music.
And where was it being performed?
